AndroidSetup.keywords: android, agp, gradle, gradlew, wrapper, kotlin, ktlint, detekt, spotless, libs-versions-toml, multi-module, verification-gates, stack-plugin, sandbox, gennadyrc
AndroidSetup.Mission:
Canonical rules for the Android/AGP toolchain layer of an SDD project: wrapper discipline, Gradle verification gates, sandboxed caches, and how an agent runs them without blowing up on a brownfield multi-module repository.
The deterministic surface is the stack plugin system: **one command — `gennady verify` — for every stack**; Android specifics live in the `android` plugin, repo specifics live in `gennady.yaml` (section `stack`; personal `.gennadyrc` deep-merges on top). Never invent per-repo Gradle wrappers or ad-hoc `./gradlew` recipes: parameterise the plugin through config instead.
**Base axiom:** a verification gate observes; it never rewrites the working tree, and it never claims a verdict about code when the tool itself failed to run.

BeliefState.Axiom:
Verification is ONE verb — `gennady verify` — regardless of stack. Different repositories differ through committed stack config (`gennady.yaml`) (gate overrides, skips, extra gates), not through different commands.
An agent that must remember `./gradlew check` here, `./gradlew app:assembleDebug` there, `make android` elsewhere will pick the wrong one. Detection chooses the plugin; config expresses the repo's deviations; the verb stays constant.

A verification gate MUST NOT modify source files.
**`./gradlew ktlintFormat` and `./gradlew spotlessApply` are forbidden as gates.** They rewrite sources in place — running them inside verification means the gate always passes and silently edits the agent's diff, destroying the phase boundary.
Use the check-only twins: `ktlintCheck`, `spotlessCheck`, `detekt`. They report offenders and exit non-zero without touching the tree. Autofix belongs in an explicit, operator-invoked fix step (post-v1 `fix` facet) — never in the gate. This applies to config-declared extraGates too: a gate that writes is a bug in the config.

Only `./gradlew` is used — never a system-installed `gradle` binary. All five wrapper files are mandatory for detection: `settings.gradle{.kts}`, `build.gradle{.kts}`, `gradlew`, `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar`, `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties`. Miss any one → detect returns `null` (not a diagnostic — same principle as a missing `go.mod`).
Corp-policy repos that keep `gradle-wrapper.jar` out of git are opted in explicitly via `stack.use: [android]` in `gennady.yaml`. Silent "half-detect" would produce ENV_FAIL on the first `./gradlew` call with a misleading expectation.

Gates run cheapest-and-most-diagnostic first: **assemble → lint → test** (base tasks `assembleDebug`, `lintDebug`, `testDebugUnitTest`) plus optional Kotlin linters (`ktlintCheck`, `detekt`, `spotlessCheck`) after lint. A compile error makes every downstream gate's output noise; still all gates execute (RUN-ALL) so one pass collects the full picture.
**Never bundle as `./gradlew check`.** The bundled aggregator hides which gate broke, disables `--only=android:lint`, and kills symmetry with `golang` (`build → vet → fmt → lint → test`) and `node` (typecheck / lint / test).

`ktlintCheck`, `detekt`, `spotlessCheck` are planned gates only when the corresponding Gradle plugin is applied — `org.jlleitschuh.gradle.ktlint`, `io.gitlab.arturbosch.detekt`, `com.diffplug.spotless`. Detection reads the root `build.gradle{.kts}` plus the AGP-holder submodule; direct or alias form via `libs.versions.toml`. Absent → gate is `skipped: `, not FAIL. Symmetrical to golang `generate` skipping when no `//go:generate` directives exist.
**Known limitation (not a diagnostic):** an optional plugin applied only in a third submodule (`:core`, `:feature/x`) is invisible to auto-detection. Operator wires it explicitly via `extraGates` in the config; scanning every submodule per detect is not worth the I/O.

Verification runs in a replica of the tree (D-STACK-013). Android declares `sandboxLinks: ['.gradle', '.kotlin']` — Gradle config-cache + daemon state, and Kotlin K2 incremental compiler metadata. These are **environment**, not tree state: they cache configuration and compiler-daemon work between runs, not compiled artifacts.
**`build/` is deliberately NOT linked.** It IS tree state (intermediate dex, R.java, .class); linking it would break fresh-clone semantics for the actual artifacts. Compromise: config-cache and K2 daemon caches yes; compiled code no. Without these two links every `verify` is a cold Gradle run (5–15 min on a mid-size project) and the agent silently learns to skip verification.

Distinguish "the tool found problems in your code" (FAIL) from "the tool could not run" (ENV_FAIL). But **AGP × JDK skew is not probed at `detect`** — the probe costs 3–8s Gradle daemon start per run and JDK toolchain semantics (`libs.versions.toml` toolchain block, `.sdkmanrc`, `.jvmrc`) is too deep to parse cheaply. Skew surfaces as an ENV_FAIL on the first `assembleDebug` with a clear Gradle message — the plugin lets Gradle self-report.
Gate-level envFail predicates (`Unsupported class file major version`, `requires JDK`, daemon crashes) still classify the outcome correctly; agents MUST NOT edit sources in response to ENV_FAIL.

Detection reads at most 32 submodules from `settings.gradle{.kts}` looking for the AGP-holder. Hitting exactly 32 without finding AGP → detect returns `null` **and** emits `ANDROID_MODULE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` diagnostic with the fix: `stack.use: [android]` + `--root=`. This is a hard I/O bound, not a policy.
A repo layout where AGP lives in the 33+-nth submodule is pathological; the escape hatch is explicit config, not silent skipping.

Gradle Version Catalog aliases are variable names — the `id` field is canonical. Real projects use `agp`, `android-app`, `androidApplication`, whatever. The plugin resolves by scanning `[plugins]` for `id = "com.android.application"` / `"com.android.library"`, taking the alias on the left, and converting `-`/`_` → `.` (TOML `android-application` → DSL `libs.plugins.android.application`).
Never hardcode alias names in configs or scripts. If a custom alias breaks detection, fix the TOML or use direct-form `id("…")` — do not paper over with `stack.use: [android]` unless the underlying assumption (wrapper present, AGP applied somewhere) actually fails.

SetupSteps.Step: Run `gennady verify --plan` from the repo root. Read: detected AGP holder module, resolved alias (if any), AGP version from `libs.versions.toml`, wrapper paths, optional-linter plugins detected, sandbox links declared, and the exact `./gradlew` argv of every gate.

For each diagnostic (missing wrapper.jar, `ANDROID_MODULE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, unresolved alias), either fix the environment or encode the deviation in `gennady.yaml` (`stack.use`, `skipGates`, `overrideGates`, `extraGates`). Never ignore one silently.

If the repo needs a non-default build variant (`assembleRelease`, `testReleaseUnitTest`), an optional linter that lives only in a third submodule, or a custom Gradle property (`-Porg.gradle.jvmargs=…`), express them as stack-config gate overrides / extraGates so every agent gets them for free.

Per-phase gate = `gennady verify` (repo-scoped for Android — Gradle owns incremental scoping via daemon + `.gradle`/`.kotlin` links). Fast inner loop = `--only=android:assemble,lint`. Full sweep on demand = `--all` (adds optional linters that were detected).

For optional linters applied only in non-detected submodules: add an explicit `extraGate` with `argv: [./gradlew, ':feature:x:ktlintCheck']` and a `timeout`. Do not rely on auto-detection outside the root + AGP-holder.

Definitions.Definition: A single verification command with a binary verdict, a working directory and captured output. Gates observe; they never mutate.
A gate outcome where the tool itself could not run (Gradle daemon crash, AGP × JDK skew, missing wrapper.jar, blocked Maven proxy). Distinct from FAIL, which is a genuine finding about the code.
The `stack` section of `gennady.yaml` / `.gennadyrc`: `use` + per-plugin `skipGates`/`overrideGates`/`extraGates`. Single point where a repo's infra deviations are declared.
Ignored paths (relative to root) symlinked into the verify replica because they carry stack execution environment, not tree state. Android: `.gradle`, `.kotlin`. Not `build/`.

The `build.gradle{.kts}` file where `com.android.application` / `com.android.library` is applied with `apply true` (direct or alias). Detection reads root first, then submodules from `settings.gradle{.kts}` (limit 32).

Pattern.Intent: See what verification would do — and what the environment is missing — before spending Gradle-daemon time on it.
Pattern.Why: Prints detection (AGP holder, alias, wrapper paths), diagnostics (module-limit, missing wrapper.jar), sandbox links, and exact gate argv. First command in any unfamiliar Android repo.

Pattern.Intent: The canonical per-phase gate. Sandboxed, non-mutating, quiet on success, stack-agnostic.
Pattern.Why: Runs `assembleDebug → lintDebug → testDebugUnitTest` plus any detected optional linters, in a replica with `.gradle`/`.kotlin` linked. RUN-ALL, SUPPRESS-ON-SUCCESS, exit 0/1/4/5.

Pattern.Intent: Encode repo-specific Android infra once, in the repo, instead of teaching every agent private commands.
Pattern.Snippet: stack: android: overrideGates: test: argv: [./gradlew, testReleaseUnitTest] timeout: 20m assemble: env: { GRADLE_OPTS: "-Xmx4g -Dorg.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx4g" } extraGates: - id: feature-x-ktlint argv: [./gradlew, ':feature:x:ktlintCheck'] timeout: 5m
Pattern.Why: Per AX_ONE_VERB_EVERY_STACK. The verb stays `gennady verify`; the config carries the differences (release variant, JVM heap, submodule-scoped linters).

Pattern.Intent: Check formatting/style without touching the working tree.
Pattern.Snippet:
# CORRECT — reports offenders, writes nothing (what the plugin plans) ./gradlew ktlintCheck spotlessCheck
# FORBIDDEN as gates — rewrite sources in place ./gradlew ktlintFormat ./gradlew spotlessApply
Pattern.Why: Per AX_GATES_NEVER_MUTATE. Autofix moves to the post-v1 `fix` facet, not into verify.

Pattern.Intent: Verify a corp-policy repo that keeps `gradle-wrapper.jar` out of git.
Pattern.Why: Per AX_WRAPPER_IS_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH. Default detection returns `null` (correct — no wrapper.jar = no wrapper). Explicit opt-in acknowledges that `./gradlew` will be materialized before verify runs (bootstrap script, CI cache) — the agent gets ENV_FAIL up front instead of a silent success.

Pattern.Intent: Cover a project whose AGP holder lives past the 32-submodule detect limit.
Pattern.Why: Per AX_MODULE_LIMIT_32. `ANDROID_MODULE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` diagnostic surfaces this; the fix is scoping the plugin to the AGP-holder module, not raising the limit.

AntiPattern.Bad: Inventing `./gradlew verify-all` / `make android-check` wrappers per repository
AntiPattern.Why: Agents must relearn the verb in every repo; knowledge does not transfer.
AntiPattern.Instead: One verb (`gennady verify`) + committed stack config for deviations.

AntiPattern.Why: Rewrites sources during verification; the gate can never fail and the diff silently grows.
AntiPattern.Instead: ./gradlew ktlintCheck / spotlessCheck / detekt (planned by the android plugin automatically when the corresponding Gradle plugin is applied).

AntiPattern.Why: Aggregator hides which gate broke, disables `--only=android:lint`, breaks symmetry with golang/node reporting.
AntiPattern.Instead: Granular plan `assembleDebug → lintDebug → testDebugUnitTest` planned automatically; the plugin reuses the Gradle daemon so 3–6 tasks share one initialization.

AntiPattern.Why: Version drift with the wrapper — silent success on one machine, mysterious FAIL on another. Corp-policy repos may also require offline reproducibility that only the pinned wrapper distribution provides.
AntiPattern.Instead: Always `./gradlew`. If missing, restore the wrapper (`gradle wrapper` bootstrap) — do not fall back to system gradle.

AntiPattern.Why: `build/` is tree state (intermediate dex, R.java, compiled .class). Linking it lets a stale artifact from a previous run produce a false PASS.
AntiPattern.Instead: Keep the declared set `['.gradle', '.kotlin']`. Cold compile per run is the correct trade — Gradle daemon + K2 incremental keep it warm enough.

AntiPattern.Why: Non-zero from Gradle can mean daemon crash, JDK skew, corrupt config-cache — not "code has issues". The agent then "fixes" healthy code.
AntiPattern.Instead: The plugin declares envFail predicates on each gate (JDK skew signatures, daemon crash markers). ENV_FAIL means fix the environment, not the code.
